summary.what_changed: Splits the previously overloaded `partial` state-tracking flag into two distinct signals: `blind` (a blocking agent was prevented from judging its input at all — e.g. source-collector, pr-summarizer, or notifier dispatch failed to produce usable output) and `degraded` (the pipeline judged its input and deliberately withheld or rejected specific content, e.g. a lint block or time-budget truncation). A run classified as blind now exits with a non-zero status code, cannot advance the watermark cursor, and is excluded from the CCE-101 auto-merge gate. Classification happens by call site rather than by matching on reason strings, and every blocking dispatch reason must now be classified — an unclassified failure defaults to blind so it fails loud instead of silently passing as green.
summary.why: Two consecutive nightly runs (31472240064 on 2026-08-11 and 31579090583 on 2026-08-12) reported `conclusion: success` in GitHub Actions even though every subagent was rate-limited and produced no output. Because the orchestrator returned 0 on every code path, this failure mode was invisible, and a subsequent run's watermark advance (PR #215) walked past three PRs (#211/#212/#213) whose documentation content is now permanently unrecoverable. CCE-144 closes that blind spot by making 'the pipeline could not judge its input' a first-class, loudly-failing state distinct from 'the pipeline judged and rejected input,' which must remain non-fatal to avoid reinstating the earlier CCE-109 doom loop.

doc_targets.notes: Document the blind vs. degraded classification, the per-call-site classification requirement, and how each flag affects exit code, watermark advance, and auto-merge eligibility.

summary.what_changed: Fixes the docs-agent's page-authoring loop so a nightly run cuts its work at a PR boundary instead of an arbitrary page-batch index. Previously the CCE-109 time-budget check fired at any batch index, and the at-least-one-progress escape hatch (`i > 0`) operated per page-batch rather than per PR. When the oldest PR in a run's window fanned out to more page batches than the time budget could author, the run split that PR's batch group on every single run and never finished authoring it — so the baseline cursor could never advance past it (observed on the ADIS host as a 20.6-day stall, always reporting `time_budget_no_advance_no_cursor`). The fix reworks the authoring loop's cut logic to operate at PR granularity: a run either fully authors a PR's page batches or defers the whole PR, guaranteeing forward progress every run.
summary.why: Root cause per CCE-152/ADIS-515: batch-level truncation combined with a batch-level (not PR-level) progress escape created a doom loop identical in spirit to CCE-109, but scoped to a single oversized PR rather than an oversized window. CCE-140's cursor-backed advance only helps once a PR is fully authored; a PR stuck mid-authoring forever blocks the cursor. Cutting authoring at PR boundaries closes that gap and lets the run's forward progress guarantees hold even for PRs with unusually large page fan-out.

doc_targets.notes: Document the PR-boundary authoring cut: the CCE-109 time-budget check and progress escape now operate per PR rather than per page-batch, closing the CCE-152 doom-loop variant.

Postmortem/decision record for the CCE-152 fix: symptom (20.6-day ADIS baseline stall, repeated time_budget_no_advance_no_cursor), root cause (batch-index cut + per-batch progress escape), and the PR-boundary authoring cut as the fix.

summary.what_changed: Fixes the citation_exists Tier-1 lint check so it resolves Python symbol citations (`path:symbol`) against any definition site — methods, nested functions, class attributes — not just top-level module definitions. Previously the linter only recognized symbols defined at the top level of a Python file, so citations to real, correctly-defined symbols nested inside a class or function were incorrectly reported as nonexistent, causing the authored page to be dropped by content-validator. Because a dropped page is not retried and the collection window still advances, this silently and permanently stranded documentation for legitimately-cited code.
summary.why: Root cause per CCE-145: on three consecutive nightly runs against theoju/claude-code-self-assessment, citation_exists produced false positives for exported symbols and gitignored paths, blocking roughly 11 authored pages per run. Because last_successful_run.head_sha advances even when a page is dropped, those pages fell permanently out of the collection range with no re-attempt path. This PR corrects the symbol-resolution logic to eliminate that class of false positive, closing CCE-145 (and is part of the broader CCE-122 line-free citation design plus the CCE-141/CCE-152 related stranding-prevention work).

summary.what_changed: The nightly orchestrator's watermark-advance logic is now cursor-backed on every code path, not just the time-truncated one. `deferred_pages_by_pr` and the `held_back` set are now computed unconditionally, and the cursor walk that limits the advance to the last fully-documented PR is entered whenever `time_truncated OR held_back` is true (previously it was nested only inside the `if time_truncated:` branch). A clean run's behavior is unchanged (full window-HEAD advance when nothing is held back); a run that is partial for a non-time reason (lint block, `page_author_invalid`, etc.) now advances only as far as the last PR whose pages all landed, instead of jumping to full window HEAD and silently discarding the undocumented window. Reason strings are now cause-dependent (`time_budget_*` vs `held_back_*`) to preserve existing operator-facing grep patterns and test assertions for the time-truncated family.
summary.why: CCE-144 built the cursor-backed advance and the `deferred_pages_by_pr` complement writer, but wired the gating check only inside the `if time_truncated:` branch. Any run that was partial for a non-time reason (a lint block or a `page_author_invalid`) fell into the `else` branch, which set `advance_sha = current_run.head_sha` (full window HEAD) without ever reading `deferred_pages_by_pr`. Because the watermark cursor is consume-once, the skipped window was permanently lost and the run still exited 0, so nothing alarmed. This was identified as a known residual ("C1") in CCE-144's own final review and documented in prose but had no ticket until CCE-151. Two incidents (runs 32460602658 and 32495019606 on 2026-08-21) each blocked a page on lint and then advanced past the very window that held the stranded content, requiring a hand-written baseline rewind to recover.

summary.what_changed: The orchestrator now detects when page-author shortens an already-resolvable citation path (e.g. dropping a leading directory segment) instead of silently letting the page get blocked by citation_exists and abandoned by the CCE-140 deferral skip. A new module, scripts/citation_repair.py, diagnoses each blocked citation and reports the most likely tracked-file candidate it was shortened from, labeling the confidence as candidate_in_run_inputs, suffix_match_only, ambiguous, or no_candidate. This diagnosis is wired into the orchestrator after the authoring loop and before the lint-block revert, and surfaces as an info-only line per blocked citation in the partial-run digest (capped per-page and per-run to avoid exceeding PR body size limits). Critically, no automatic repair or rewrite of the page is performed — after four adversarial review rounds each found a new way that mutating the page could move a citation into a region citation_exists does not verify, turning a correct BLOCK into a silent PASS even after the cited file was deleted. The capability that would have caused that class of defect was deleted rather than patched again.
summary.why: CCE-141: page-author occasionally emits a shortened, non-resolving citation for a path that was originally valid (the ADIS page's `.claude/skills/connector-builder/references/checklist.md` became bare `references/checklist.md`). citation_exists correctly blocks it, but post-CCE-140 that block causes the deferral skip to abandon the PR, so the page is never written and the problem is invisible. An automatic repair-and-rewrite mechanism was built and reviewed four times to fix this, but every round found the same underlying flaw in a new disguise — repair could relocate a citation into a lint blind spot, converting a correct block into an unverified false pass. Production evidence showed zero real-world firings for a valid repair candidate and the full test suite stayed green with the repair path disabled, so the decision was to ship detection-only: report the likely intended file and let a human resolve it, rather than risk silent corruption for an unmeasured benefit.

doc_targets.notes: Documents the CCE-141 decision: shortened-citation detection ships as diagnosis-only (scripts/citation_repair.py), with automatic repair explicitly rejected after four adversarial review rounds each surfacing a new BLOCK-to-silent-PASS corruption path. summary.what_changed: Fixes the citation-shortening diagnostic run cap in the orchestrator so it recovers state from a typed counter instead of parsing its own rendered digest text. Any rename of that prefix would silently disable the `_CITATION_RUN_FINDINGS_CAP` bound with no test failure to catch it. The fix decouples the cap's state from the formatter's output string.

summary.what_changed: Fixes a docstring/behavior mismatch in state_io.save_current_run: the per-run current_run.json sibling was documented as gitignored and excluded from the merge-as-promotion path, which is only true in the plugin's own repo (its .gitignore lists the file). On a host repo, which does not inherit that .gitignore entry, the orchestrator's git add -A staging would commit this ephemeral per-run state file into every docs PR. The fix corrects the docstring and makes the invariant true at onboarding by having setup gitignore the current_run.json sibling on host repos, not just in this repo.

Since _stage_docs_run_changes uses git add -A, this silently committed ephemeral run state into host docs PRs. Related history in CCE-70 and CCE-75 shows this is a recurring class of bug (unguarded broad git add picking up paths hosts don't already exclude), so this PR closes the gap by making onboarding/setup gitignore the sibling on hosts as well as correcting the docstring.
